newsitem.title: INDIA: Indonesia sees sugar expansion outside Java.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees sugar expansion outside Java.

text.p: Indonesia is looking to expand its sugar industry in areas outside the main island of Java, a senior Indonesian industry official said on Tuesday.
Faruk Bakrie, chairman of the Indonesian Sugar Association, said almost 70 percent of national production came from Java.
"The expansion of the sugar industry in the future will be based on the expansion off Java," he told the Asia International Sugar Conference in New Delhi.
Bakrie said farmland on and around Java was not readily available because of rapid population growth and increased competition from the non-farm sector.
"Cane farming itself is facing competition with the rice farming, which is more profitable," he said.
He said between 1975 and 1995 domestic sugar production rose at an average 5.11 percent per year.
Bakrie said the government some years ago launched an output expansion programme by establishing sugar mills outside Java.
"In the past few years, sugar imports were successively decreased but sugar self-sufficiency was still not achievable," Bakrie said.
Indonesia produced 2.09 million tonnes of sugar in 1995, down from 2.4 million the previous year. The fall was due to a long dry spell, he said.
Bakrie said the area under cane cultivation rose to 433,610 hectares in 1995 from 104,780 in 1975.
At the same time, production rose by a narrower margin to 2.09 million tonnes from 1.03 million.
"The Indonesian sugar industry has to continually strive for efforts to reduce costs of production by increasing the productivity," Bakrie said.
